entries.name: goose-acme
entries.description: Obtains and renews TLS certificates from Let's Encrypt or another ACME authority via TLS-ALPN-01, so a goose-http server can serve HTTPS with no reverse proxy.

entries.name: goose-http
entries.description: The most complete HTTP server stack for Goose: per-worker event loops on io_uring, epoll, kqueue or IOCP, with WebSockets, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, static files and an outbound client. Upstream benchmarks against it.

entries.name: goose-web
entries.description: A web framework built on a non-blocking readiness loop, with typed routes, JSON validation, HTML templates, streaming responses and an optional SQLite layer.

entries.name: honk
entries.description: A web framework where routes declare typed structs and the request parsing, validation, JSON responses and OpenAPI schema with Swagger UI follow from those types.

entries.name: goose-tls
entries.description: TLS on OpenSSL 3: a TLS 1.3 server whose protocol layer is Goose (with OpenSSL's libcrypto for primitives) and OpenSSL's own client, both byte-in, byte-out with kTLS support.

entries.name: goose-postgres
entries.description: A PostgreSQL client that speaks protocol 3.0 as bytes in and bytes out, leaving sockets to the caller's event loop; it handles SCRAM login, pipelined queries and result decoding, and pairs with goose-http's loop.

entries.name: goose-sqlite
entries.description: SQLite with the amalgamation built in, so no system SQLite is needed. Errors surface through Goose's return-from, and the compiler checks every call runs inside a transaction or run block.

entries.name: goose-sqlite
entries.description: A second SQLite binding with the amalgamation vendored in, written for and used by the Swan code-map tool, with a small self-contained test script.

entries.name: goose-compress
entries.description: Compression encoders for gzip, zlib, raw DEFLATE and zstd, mostly Goose with a few C hot loops, including a flushing streaming mode; goose-http uses it for responses.

entries.name: goose-deflate
entries.description: DEFLATE decoding of all block types plus a simple encoder (fixed Huffman or stored blocks), with zlib and gzip framing.

entries.name: goose-inflate
entries.description: A streaming DEFLATE and gzip decoder in pure Goose that you feed compressed chunks of any size, with caller-owned fixed-size state and CRC-32.

entries.name: goose-tar
entries.description: A push-style tar reader for ustar, GNU and PAX archives that takes input in arbitrary chunks and reports headers and data through a callback; decompression is left to you.

entries.name: goose-zip
entries.description: Walks a ZIP file held in memory and hands back entry names and payloads as slices into it; pair it with a DEFLATE decoder for compressed entries.

entries.name: lz78-goose
entries.description: A small LZ78 compressor with a documented format, a Python cross-check and a Windows archiver CLI; the author presents it as a learning project about Goose's memory model.

entries.name: goose-libdeflate
entries.description: libdeflate compiled into the package: fast whole-buffer zlib, gzip and raw DEFLATE in both directions, plus CRC-32 and Adler-32. Tags track the libdeflate version.

entries.name: asn1goose
entries.description: A strict, zero-copy ASN.1 DER reader and writer with typed decoders and PEM support; the base of the same author's X.509 and TLS packages.

entries.name: goose-layout
entries.description: Reads and writes fixed-layout binary headers straight into Goose structs field by field, big- or little-endian, all-or-nothing.

entries.name: goose-msgpack
entries.description: MessagePack reading and writing that picks the shortest integer forms and keeps map pairs in insertion order.

entries.name: goose-toml
entries.description: A TOML 1.0 reader that fills a caller-owned node tree and reports a bad document as an error message.

entries.name: goose-uuid
entries.description: Generates, parses and formats RFC 9562 UUIDs of versions 1 through 8, accepting the common text forms including URNs.

entries.name: serialize.goose
entries.description: A bit-packing serializer for game and network messages that produces exactly the same bytes as the C and C++ serialize libraries, covering every field type they support.
